id: title:eli-r-ph:ignore an out of range offset instead of panicking

review.posthog_relevance: Stability and recovery of the Person identity replication layer (`rust/personhog-replica/`) against client-supplied timestamp overflow, preventing request aborts and preserving batch integrity.
review.reason: The chunk P1.F1.H1 replaces an unchecked timestamp subtraction with a bounded, checked arithmetic sequence, preventing a potential panic and request abort when client-supplied offsets exceed representable ranges. P1.F1.H2 adds a regression test specifically targeting this failure mode. This demonstrates a substantive, bounded correctness and reliability improvement rather than a 3,
review.uncertainty: The broader system-wide impact and complete recovery behavior are not fully demonstrated; the benefit is inferred from the local implementation and test, not from observed production outcomes.

observations.limitations: This chunk contains two hunks. P1.F1.H1 shows a change from a direct subtraction to a safe, checked arithmetic sequence, and P1.F1.H2 adds a regression test. No other hunks are supplied, so no broader context or related changes can be assessed. No score is assigned.

observations.behavior: Replaces a direct subtraction with a safe, checked arithmetic sequence; the previous implementation could panic if the client-supplied offset, when subtracted from the current time, exceeded the representable range of the timestamp type. The new implementation uses Duration::try_milliseconds and checked_sub_signed, returning None and preserving the current time rather than panicing
observations.posthog_connection: This protects the Rust PersonHog replica, which stores person identities and their associated timestamps. A client sending an out-of-range offset could previously cause a panic, potentially aborting the request and losing the batch. observations.behavior: Adds a regression test exercising the exact failure mode: an offset that, when subtracted, would exceed the representable range. The test asserts that the result preserves the current time and does not panic, and also checks that a client-provided timestamp still overrides the offset even when the offset is out of range.
observations.posthog_connection: This test could help prevent future regressions where a change to the timestamp parsing or arithmetic could re-introduce a panic or incorrect behavior. It could also help catch edge cases where the offset and client timestamp interact unexpectedly.
